flawed_step: The universal existence claim fails when n=6.
counterexample: Take n=6. A simple graph on 6 vertices has 15 possible edges. If G has m edges, its complement has 15-m edges. Isomorphic graphs have equal numbers of edges, so self-complementarity would require m=15-m, hence 2m=15. This is impossible because m is an integer. Therefore no self-complementary graph on 6 vertices exists.
assessment_summary: Proof attempt: (1) If G is self-complementary, G and its complement have equal edge counts. (2) Thus 2|E(G)|=n(n-1)/2. (3) For n=6 this becomes 2|E(G)|=15, an impossibility. Since 6>=4, this concrete obstruction refutes the statement.
